newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to keep cutting French jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Renault to keep cutting French jobs - paper.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a newspaper interview that the car company would keep cutting jobs in France at a rate of around 3,000 a year.
"There's going to be a reduction of jobs in Europe," he said in an interview in the afternoon newspaper Le Monde.

"Productivity is increasing by six to seven percent a year, and the market by three percent. There's a gap. This year we're cutting close to 6,000 jobs in France and Belgium. We're on a trend of 3,000 job cuts a year in France," Schweitzer said.
Workers are already fighting plans to close a Belgian plant in Vilvoorde and cut 2,764 jobs in France this year.

Some 30 Belgian workers protesting the plant closure camped at a car depot in the town of Wavrin in northern France on Thursday night to block deliveries of vehicles, including Renault cars, to dealers.
Taking several thousand cars "hostage", they plan to remain there until Monday morning.

Belgian workers pelted police with stones at Wavrin on Thursday and police fired tear gas in the roughest protest to date against Renault's cost-cutting plans. Police kept a discreet presence on Friday.
The company reported a 5.25 billion franc ($920.4 million) loss on Thursday, including 3.91 billion for restructuring charges.
Over the past 10 years it has cut staff by 40,000 to just under 141,000 at the end of 1996.
